title: Beyond Gonad Yield: Metabolic Plasticity of Paracentrotus lividus Under Diet, Cultivation, and Natural Temporal Variation
content: The biochemical quality of sea urchin gonads depends on diet, reproductive physiology, sex, and environment, yet these factors are rarely assessed together. We investigated gonadal metabolic plasticity in Paracentrotus lividus by combining phenotypic measurements with polar and apolar ¹H NMR profiling. Twenty-four urchins entered a 29-day 2 × 2 factorial feeding trial (terrestrial vegetable by-products or macroalgae, with or without mussel supplementation; 21 reached the endpoint), alongside independent wild animals sampled at three times (n = 13, 13, 12). Wild groups showed pronounced cross-sectional variation in gonadosomatic index (GSI), polar metabolism, and relative lipid composition: glycine tracked GSI, formate retained a temporal effect after GSI adjustment, alanine was sex-associated, and glycerol/TAG-associated regions showed strong temporal and sex structure. Female-only and centered log-ratio analyses supported these associations, indicating robustness to unequal sex ratios and compositional closure constraints. Diet effects were weak; base-associated L0 and L2 differences were sensitive to compositional transformation and to formulation, and no mussel or interaction effect was detected. Cultivated gonads differed markedly from wild gonads, with taurine and the L4 and L5 lipid regions most consistent; taurine and L4 remained robust across adjustments and comparators, whereas formate was comparator-dependent. Gonadal mass, polar metabolism, and relative lipid composition are related but non-equivalent dimensions of gonadal physiology, supporting metabolomic profiling alongside conventional production traits in echinoculture.
